svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: The Intelligence Index froze, so the race moved to serving speed — three ways past the memory wall
svg.desc: A horizontal bar chart of output tokens per second on a logarithmic scale for three ways of serving a model. A GPU-served frontier model runs at roughly 100 tokens per second and is labelled the status quo, bottlenecked by fetching weights from memory — the memory wall. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast tier, powered by Cerebras wafer-scale chips and previewed August 13, runs at 750 tokens per second, about 14 times standard, but still has no published price or general-availability date. Taalas HC1, the etched-silicon startup AMD agreed to acquire on August 6, runs Llama 8B at 16,960 tokens per second, roughly 48 times a GPU, by burning the weights permanently into the circuit so there is no memory fetch — at the cost that one chip can run only the one model it was fabricated for, and only a small 8-billion-parameter model has been shown. A caption notes that the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ceiling is frozen for a sixth straight brief — Claude Opus 5 at 63 and still number one and uncut, Fable 5 at 62.1, Grok 4.6 at 60.9, with no Index-64 model and no flagship price cut since July 24 — so competition has shifted from how smart to how fast.
svg.text: The Index froze, so the race moved to speed — three ways past the memory wall
Output tokens/sec (log scale) · serving-stack throughput as of Aug 2026 · not size-matched (see notes)
❄ Intelligence Index frozen 6th brief — Opus 5 63 (#1, uncut) · Fable 5 62.1 · Grok 4.6 60.9 · no Index-64, no flagship cut since Jul 24
status quo · weights fetched from HBM each step — the memory wall
~14× standard · preview since Aug 13 · still no price, no GA date
Taalas HC1 — weights etched into silicon (AMD acq. Aug 6)
~48× a GPU · no memory fetch — the weights ARE the circuit · but one chip = one model (shown on Llama-8B only)
Motion this window is on the horizontal axis, not the vertical one: labs compete on latency because the Index and prices haven't moved in ~4 weeks.
